description: The shared agent identity line: the agent's initials (or its picture) on the agent's palette colour, the name, and — when the host reports one — the activity state as an icon, a WORD and a tone. Every agent visualization (lanes, graph, fan-out, handoff, presence roster) renders this component, so an agent looks the same wherever it appears and its state is never colour-only information (WCAG 1.4.1). The colour comes from AgentRef.ColorIndex, which is normalised into the eight-slot palette --tm-agent-color-0 … --tm-agent-color-7; the ink painted on it is --tm-agent-color-ink, whose AA (4.5:1) contrast against every slot is measured in both themes by AgentColorTokenTests. The picture is host data: AgentRef.AvatarUrl is loaded only when it is an absolute http(s) source (the package's image allowlist, the same rule the markdown pipeline applies to images) and a refused target falls back to the initials instead of becoming a live source or a broken image. The badge is NOT a live region, carries no aria-live and never moves (no transition, no animation): the surface that owns the run has exactly one announcement channel, and a pulsing badge would become a second one while re-introducing motion that prefers-reduced-motion would have to cover. Naming: with the name visible the badge has no aria-label at all — the visible text IS the accessible name (WCAG 2.5.3); with ShowName=false the composed avatar becomes one role="img" graphic named by the agent and, when one is rendered, its state, because an aria-label on a role-less span is ignored by assistive technology. An unknown state value renders no chip, so a stale contract can never paint a wrong verdict, and a whitespace name renders the localized "Unnamed agent" fallback instead of an empty gap.

parameters.name: Agent
parameters.description: The agent to show. Null renders nothing at all — a surface that has not loaded its snapshot yet must not paint an anonymous avatar. The record is a VALUE: a host recomposes it with `agent with { … }`.

parameters.name: Status
parameters.description: What the agent is doing right now. Null (the default) renders no state chip at all, which is not the same as Idle. A value the component cannot name (an enum member from a newer backend) also renders no chip, so a stale contract can never paint a wrong verdict.

parameters.name: ShowName
parameters.description: Whether the agent's name is rendered next to the avatar. Default true. With false the badge becomes one labelled graphic (role="img") named by the agent and its state.

parameters.name: ShowStatus
parameters.description: Whether the state chip is rendered when Status is set. Default true. Turning it off is how a dense surface (a graph node, an attempt tile) keeps the state on its own row instead of inside the badge.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: Avatar and text size: Sm (20 px), Md (24 px, the default) or Lg (32 px). The size sets one component knob, so the initials cannot drift from the circle that contains them.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: AdditionalAttributes
parameters.description: Additional HTML attributes applied to the root element.

parameters.name: DataTestId
parameters.description: Overrides the root data-testid (default "agent-badge", namespaced by TestIdPrefix).

parameters.name: TestIdPrefix
parameters.description: Namespaces every internal data-testid of this instance, so several badges on one page stay targetable.

examples.title: A running agent in a lane header
examples.code:
<TmAgentBadge Agent="planner" Status="AgentActivityStatus.Running" />

@code {
    private readonly AgentRef planner = new("Planner", "agent-planner")
    {
        Role = "Orchestrator",
        ColorIndex = 0,
    };
}

examples.title: An avatar-only badge inside a graph node or a table cell
The colour comes from the palette slot, not from the host

notes: The badge is deliberately not interactive: it renders no button, no tab stop and no drag surface, so WCAG 2.5.7's non-drag alternative and the 44 px coarse-pointer target do not apply to it — a host that makes a whole row clickable keeps that obligation on its own row. Its CSS declares no transition or animation, which keeps the package's reduced-motion enumeration unchanged; a future animated subject has to add its own prefers-reduced-motion block. Under Windows high contrast the avatar opts out of the system palette (forced-color-adjust: none) so the eight agent fills stay distinguishable and keeps a CanvasText border for the circle's edge.
